challenge.name: The Heatwave Blind Spot
challenge.description: A sudden heatwave has shifted demand for seasonal articles, and the current forecast is missing the mark. #model_monica# wants to automate the evaluation harness to test new weather features rapidly, while #requirements_reuben# wants to keep it manual to ensure every test case is rigorously documented before any model change is considered.

output.content: We are losing valuable sprint cycles watching hyperparameter tuning run by hand. The current process is slow and consumes significant engineering time that could be spent on feature engineering. I am prepared to accept a manual approach to tuning, provided the evaluation harness itself is rapid. If the evaluation loop is fast enough, the lack of automation in the tuning step is a cost I can absorb. The trade is clear: we give up the convenience of automated tuning in exchange for a system that lets us validate new weather features quickly. This balance protects our timeline for the upcoming promotion season while acknowledging the current resource constraints.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are prepared to give up the convenience of automated tuning in exchange for a rapid evaluation harness, defining a clear trade-off.
